name: Frostline Gear Arctic Thermal Underlayer
description:
A heavyweight thermal base layer designed for sub-zero outdoor operations. The fabric is triple-layered — moisture-wicking inner, insulating middle, wind-blocking outer. The suit covers everything from ankles to wrists to neck, with thumb loops to prevent sleeve ride-up under gloves.

Designed for external infrastructure maintenance crews who work on exposed upper-tier structures during winter. The Arctic Underlayer is the difference between a four-hour shift and hypothermia, and the crews who wear it treat it with the respect given to equipment that keeps them alive.
functionality: Extreme cold insulation, moisture management, wind resistance
what_it_says: The cold would kill you without this and you wear it like a second skin because it nearly is one.
story_hooks: A winter maintenance crew's thermal underlayers are found to have been contaminated with a contact irritant — someone wanted the crew to strip their cold protection during a sub-zero shift.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, form-fitting full-body thermal suit that hugs the silhouette while creating subtle dimensional layering. The garment presents as a unified thermal cocoon — high neckline, long tapered sleeves with integrated thumb loops, and ankle-length legs. Despite its technical function, it maintains clean minimalist aesthetics with subtle ribbed texture breaks.
physical_description.fit: Compression-adjacent but not restrictive; snug enough to maximize heat retention and minimize air pockets, with articulated panels at joints (shoulders, elbows, knees) allowing full mobility. Engineered for layering under bulkier protective gear.
physical_description.primary_material: Triple-layer synthetic composite: inner moisture-wicking microfiber (hydrophobic treatment), middle thermal-retention foam (aerogel-infused), outer wind-blocking ballistic weave with DWR coating
physical_description.texture: Smooth inner surface with subtle grid quilting visible through the outer layer; the outer face has a soft matte finish with micro-dimple texture for water shedding. Thumb loop cuffs are reinforced with friction-grip ribbing.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep arctic blue-gray base with charcoal thermal gradient panels along spine, shoulder blades, and outer thighs. Subtle reflective piping at seams (safety visibility in snow glare). Frostline Gear branding in minimal white serif text at sternum.
physical_description.closures: Full-length rear zipper with thermally-insulated slider and internal wind baffle. Magnetic snap closure at neck to prevent zipper failure in extreme cold. Thumb loops are friction-fit elastic.
distinctive_features: Integrated thumb loops prevent sleeve creep under external gloves
Taped seams throughout to eliminate thermal leakage points
Reinforced panel zones (shoulders, lower back, calves) with secondary insulation layer
Subtle Frostline Gear geometric logo — a stylized snowflake/thermal wave pattern
Heat-mapped color gradation suggesting insulation density distribution
Interior neck tag with manufacturing date and thermal rating (rated -40°C to -65°C operational)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 functional luxury. Expensive enough to signal corporate affiliation or specialized trade credential, yet purely utilitarian in design. Not aspirational fashion — this is survival equipment that costs what it costs because lives depend on it.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by external infrastructure maintenance crews, aerial scaffold workers, and upper-tier structure repair specialists. Signals dangerous, cold-exposure work on the GLMZ's highest platforms. Also worn by enthusiasts of extreme-environment recreation. The garment says: 'I work where it kills the unprepared.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine or slightly broken-in when new; with use, develops subtle creasing at joints and minor discoloration from sweat salt. Well-maintained specimens show no damage; damaged units (torn seams, zipper failure, thermal degradation) are immediately replaced — equipment failure = medical emergency.
